name: color-picker
pattern: A named group for editing a color in a specified-gamut HSVA model. Operate the square color area and hue wheel with native buttons and each channel with native ranges. Do not create a two-dimensional slider role or application role
responsibility: Manage one color, synchronization between direct manipulation and native controls, color and channel values readable by CSS, cancelable commit events, connection, and form reset. The user provides the HTML, color surfaces, handles, gradients, labels, and placement
relationship: area, wheel, and channel sliders are different interaction entry points for the same color and are not separate controllers. Existing slider state is a single native-range value or a start/end pair, while this controller is a named group whose state is the entire color including its color space. Native input[type=color] does not provide two-axis editing in the page and has engine differences in preserving alpha / colorspace. Refer to measurements in native_color.test.ts and fixtures/native_color_observations.json

authorMarkup.root: An HTMLElement with data-controller="color-picker" and role="group". Do not use a button/input/select/textarea itself as the root. Name its purpose with aria-label or aria-labelledby

targets.area: Zero or one native button[type=button] that operates the whole saturation × brightness square. Give it a name that makes movement to channel controls with Enter / Space clear
targets.wheel: Zero or one native button[type=button] that selects hue from an angle on the color surface. Give it a name that makes movement to the hue control with Enter / Space clear
targets.hueControl: One named native input[type=range]. min=0, max=360, step=any. The unit is degrees
targets.saturationControl: One named native input[type=range]. min=0, max=100, step=any. The unit is %
targets.brightnessControl: One named native input[type=range]. min=0, max=100, step=any. The unit is %
targets.alphaControl: One named native input[type=range]. min=0, max=1, step=any. 0 is transparent and 1 is opaque
targets.instructions: Exactly one is required when area or wheel exists; otherwise zero or one. A non-empty HTMLElement describing direct arrow, Shift, Escape, and Enter/Space interactions and native range positions. Do not reuse the root or another target, and place it outside the handle

authorMarkup.composition: All configurations require four ranges. Allow range-only, area, wheel, and area-plus-wheel configurations. Every target must be a distinct descendant of the root; do not nest buttons or put ranges / instructions inside a button. Do not hide ranges or set aria-hidden; use CSS that makes every track clickable and tappable. When ranges are grouped in details, preserve a structure that reaches every control from summary
authorMarkup.names: Name each range with a label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. Verify that label.control references the input. Name each button with text, aria-label, or aria-labelledby. aria-labelledby requires a non-empty reference target. The controller does not infer names or descriptions
authorMarkup.relations: area aria-controls references the IDs of saturationControl and brightnessControl; wheel references the ID of hueControl. The user keeps replacement control IDs and authored relationship attributes consistent. Compose instructions into aria-describedby
authorMarkup.form: All range form owners must be the same form or all null. The user writes name and any hidden input required to submit the color space. Native ranges submit each number. The full color CSS string is available from the public color getter. The controller does not generate a hidden input
authorMarkup.css: Use a horizontal writing mode for area and wheel with no border / padding and no rotation, skew, or inversion transform. For area, saturation 0 is inline-start and 100 inline-end; brightness 100 is the top and 0 the bottom. For wheel, hue 0 is at the top and increases clockwise; do not reverse direction in RTL. The user sets touch-action to none on the handle. Use output values to draw surfaces and handles; the controller does not directly set position, dimension, or color properties. Keep P3 as CSS color(display-p3 ...)

semanticElements: The root and every target satisfy the authorMarkup counts, containment, element types, names, relationships, and range bounds
An explicit root role is group, a handle role is button, and a range role is slider. Use native semantics when roles are omitted
Check the handle's horizontal writing mode, finite settings, and value shape
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate initially and when targets or settings change. If invalid, do not partially apply completion; disable enhancement and issue one warning in English while connected. If a valid configuration becomes invalid, cancel the preview, restore old output to the committed value, and remove listeners. For initially invalid markup, do not write state or CSS. Revalidate after the target or settings are repaired

completion.warning: List the completed attributes and issue the warning "Added <attributes>. Include them in your markup." once while connected. Use a separate flag from the disabling warning

completionExempt: Composition of the instructions ID into aria-describedby
Synchronization of range.value with state and CSS custom properties
contractValidation.preservation: Do not overwrite authored IDs or static attributes. Verify that min/max use the HTML valid floating-point number syntax and equal the contract values, and that step is any. Use native values without adding aria-valuenow/min/max to ranges. Do not change disabled

value.description: Initial ColorPickerValue. Apply a bulk change as a new value. Reject invalid JSON, shape, color space, or non-finite numbers and retain the last committed value

step.description: The percentage step for saturation and brightness changed by area arrows. Greater than 0 and at most 100

hueStep.description: The degree step for hue changed by wheel arrows. Greater than 0 and at most 360

value.description: A copy of the committed color. ColorPickerValue has colorSpace: srgb | display-p3, hue:0..360, saturation:0..100, brightness:0..100, and alpha:0..1. The setter validates four finite numbers and the color space, clamps out-of-range values, invalidates the preview, and commits without notification or focus movement. Invalid values and calls while disconnected are no-ops. null before the first valid connection

color.description: Returns the committed color as color(srgb r g b / a) or color(display-p3 r g b / a). RGB uses encoded components 0..1 in each color space and is derived from HSVA. Do not round to 8-bit or reduce P3 to sRGB. null before the first valid connection

color-picker:beforechange.when: Immediately before commitment from a trusted direct pointerup, handle arrow, or native range change. A trusted input without an origin, such as AT input, commits once
color-picker:beforechange.detail: ColorPickerChangeDetail = { value: ColorPickerValue; previousValue: ColorPickerValue; color: string; reason: pointer | keyboard; source: area | wheel | hue | saturation | brightness | alpha }
color-picker:beforechange.effect: preventDefault stops commitment and change and restores all output to the committed value before the change. API, settings, target, disabled, or connection changes in a listener take precedence over the candidate; do not apply an old candidate

color-picker:change.when: After committing the change and synchronizing all output
color-picker:change.detail: The same ColorPickerChangeDetail as beforechange. Do not share the object between internal state, before, and after

events.preview: pointermove and range input with an origin emit preview only. The public getter returns the committed value. Do not emit either event for an equal-value commitment. Distinguish hue 0 and 360 as channel values even when their RGB is equal
events.reason: Use pointer when direct pointer or range pointerdown is the origin; use keyboard for keydown or an originless native AT adjustment. Do not notify for programmatic changes, reset, reconnection, or cancellation
events.synthetic: Ignore pointer, keydown, and click with isTrusted=false. For synthetic input/change, return to current output values and do not notify even if only the native value changes

behavior.model: HSVA represents the encoded RGB cube of the specified color space. Preserve hue for achromatic saturation=0 and brightness=0 so it is not lost when saturation or brightness increases again. Interpret assignment of a value including colorSpace as a new color; do not perform automatic color-space conversion or gamut mapping. The browser drawing CSS owns gamut mapping for the display
behavior.configuration: Save the first valid value as the form-reset snapshot. A value-attribute change applies the latest input in bulk; a step-only change and reconnection retain the current committed value. Read values through Stimulus values and catch JSON errors. Settings and target changes cancel an operation in progress
behavior.direct: Capture area/wheel only for a primary-pointer left button and use pointer position as the preview. Clamp area coordinates to 0..100 and reverse the saturation axis in RTL. Convert the angle of the vector from the normalized center into clockwise 0..360 with 0 at the top for wheel. Preserve the existing hue at the center point. Commit once at the final pointerup coordinates. A stationary click or tap can select a value through the same path. Do not start when capture fails or dimensions are zero or non-finite
behavior.cancellation: Discard the preview on pointercancel, unexpected lostpointercapture, Escape, window blur, surface rectangle/direction/disabled changes, settings changes, target replacement, the public setter, reset, or disconnect. Do not mix events from another pointer. Ordinary capture release after pointerup does not cancel commitment
behavior.nativeRange: Preserve native keyboard, track click, drag, and AT input. Take a starting snapshot on pointerdown or the corresponding keydown, preview on input, and commit on change. A trusted originless input/change commits as one keyboard operation and does not notify twice on a subsequent equal change. keyup/pointerup wait for native change and return to idle when equal. Cancel the preview if change has not completed before blur
behavior.staleRange: Return remaining input/change from a native range operation invalidated by an API, settings, target change, reset, or similar action to the current value. Release the invalidation record in the next task after a new trusted pointerdown/keydown or physical operation ends. If pointerup/keyup is lost, release it in the next task after trusted focus resumes on the range or window, or after a pointermove with buttons=0. Exclude an old completion delivered in the same task as focus resumption, and accept originless AT adjustments thereafter. Remove delayed processing on disconnect
behavior.activation: When area/wheel is activated by Enter/Space or an originless trusted click, move focus from area to enabled saturationControl, or brightnessControl if unavailable; move focus from wheel to enabled hueControl. Open closed ancestor details from the outside inward. A click immediately after selecting a color with the pointer does not move focus this way
behavior.disabled: Read native disabled and ancestor-fieldset disabled with :disabled. A disabled handle stops only its direct manipulation. A disabled range also fixes that channel against direct manipulation. If only one area channel is disabled, the other still moves. Cancel all previews when disabled state changes during an operation. The public setter remains usable regardless of disabled
behavior.reset: For reset of the form owning the four ranges, check defaultPrevented after dispatch and return to the initial snapshot in a task after native reset. A canceled reset changes nothing, including the preview. API, settings, target, and disconnect changes after scheduling take precedence and are not overwritten by an old schedule. Do not dispatch events or move focus
behavior.nested: Separate targets of same-type controllers by Stimulus scope and verify ownership of the current target when processing events. Users receiving notifications outside narrow them with :self or event.target===event.currentTarget

area.ArrowLeft: Decrease saturation by 1 step visually to the left (increase in RTL)
area.ArrowRight: Decrease saturation by 1 step visually to the right (decrease in RTL)

wheel.ArrowRight: Increase hue by hueStep (decrease in RTL)
wheel.ArrowLeft: Decrease hue by hueStep (increase in RTL)

handles.Control: Ignore custom key operations while modified
handles.Alt: Ignore custom key operations while modified
handles.Meta: Ignore custom key operations while modified

stateOutputs.root: Emit root data-state=idle | adjusting and data-color-space=srgb | display-p3. The whole color has one interaction state and color space. The color space can also be used to choose the CSS interpolation method. Do not add disabled or per-channel boundary states
stateOutputs.properties: Emit unitless --color-picker-hue (degrees), --color-picker-saturation / --color-picker-brightness (0..1), --color-picker-alpha (0..1), --color-picker-color (the selected color() string), and --color-picker-hue-color (a color() string in the same color space and hue with saturation, brightness, and alpha set to 1) on the root. During preview use the candidate; otherwise use the committed value. Do not convert the color space to sRGB
stateOutputs.controls: Synchronize the values of four native ranges to the same HSVA value. min/max/step are completion targets; do not write aria-valuenow/min/max separately

lifecycle: Target callbacks are also called before connect, so do not set listeners or output before connection
Remove all root, document, window, and form listeners, the settings observer, pointer capture, and reset and stale-record timers in disconnect
Do not duplicate registrations on reconnection; revalidate the latest markup and current value. Old targets and callbacks have no effect
disconnect discards the preview and retains committed-value output and generated attributes. Do not move focus with a timer

observations.environment: Safari + VoiceOver, Firefox + NVDA, touch devices, and Display-P3 displays
observations.item: Group names, four range values and instructions, native AT adjustment, touch drag/track tap, and P3 rendering
observations.impact: Named native controls always provide an equivalent route. Geometry, roles, and public values are fixed; headless screenshots do not verify physical P3 rendering.

acceptanceCriteria: Require WCAG 2.2 Level AA for every configuration. Preserve the name, values, and operations of the named group and native button/range, and do not represent two axes with a single aria-valuenow
AAA 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception): the area axes, wheel hue, and every channel can be operated by keyboard. AAA 3.2.5 Change on Request: move focus only from user activation and never from a timer
WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.7: directly test area/wheel clicks and taps and track clicks on every native range in all three engines. Keyboard equivalents alone do not pass
Preserve every encoded component range of sRGB and Display-P3 and alpha0..1; do not replace P3 primary red with sRGB red. Test CSS color() color-space tags and channels in a real browser
Test direct operations, native operations, cancellation, reentrancy, invalid markup, dynamic targets, reset, RTL, multiple instances, and synthetic events in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Place a negative control for each guard and verify that the targeted test fails and the source is restored

observation (unverified): observe group/name, four-range values, operation instructions, and native AT adjustments with Safari+VoiceOver, Firefox+NVDA, and similar combinations. An equivalent path to native controls always exists, and public specifications do not depend on observations. Touch-device drag and track tap and color rendering on P3-capable displays are also unverified compatibility observations. Do not treat headless screenshots as evidence of P3 color rendering

testMatrix.description: Two axes, wheel, RTL, modifiers, and IME
Preview and commitment for clicks and drag
Native range keyboard, track, and drag
Cancellation of before and in-progress operations
Priority of API, settings, and target reentrancy
Disabled state including fieldsets and fixed channels
Validation and completion of semantics, names, and values
Disconnected, replaced, restored, and invalidated input
Native reset cancellation, delay, and generations
Isolation of nested same-type controllers and multiple roots
